forecaster_note: Surf Guru read: a solid mid-period south swell is on the coast — 7.2ft @ 10s from 179° at Long Reef, 6.3ft @ 11s from 180° down at North Steyne. Dead south again, which is the angle Dee Why hates: the headland eats it, so the exposed banks do all the work. Long Reef is the standout at 6–8ft (overhead to well overhead) and rates FAIR; Curl Curl runs 4–6ft; Dee Why sits around 4–5ft; North Steyne is shadowed right down to 2–3ft+ and only rates poor-to-fair. The wind was the whole story and it has already turned — clean W offshore at dawn, SW by mid-morning, and by 11:40am it is 6–8kt SSW–SSE, cross to lightly onshore. Surfline's Jax Richards: 'South swell magnets the pick of it with largest size early. Morning winds best bet… Morning session is cleanest with afternoon winds going lightly onshore & staying manageable.' The 9:22am high has passed and it drains to a 2:53pm low, so the banks get shallower through the afternoon. Water 18.3°C, air 17°C — still a 3/2 and boots morning. Surfline flags more south swell inbound for NSW this weekend. ✈️ Reminder: you're in Oahu until 13 Aug — this whole run happens without you, run /hawaii-surf over there instead. ⚠️ Data note: Dee Why and Curl Curl could not be refreshed directly this run (Surfline served a stale cached page for Dee Why and returned empty for Curl Curl, and the Surfline JSON API was unreachable) — both are estimated from live neighbouring-spot readings. Nearshore energy (kJ) and consistency are unavailable this run. 🦈 SharkSmart could not be read this refresh — no all-clear should be assumed, tap through to check live detections. — Surfline Sydney forecast (Jax Richards / Hugh McDowell)

wind.summary: Clean W offshore at first light, SW through mid-morning, and by late morning it has swung SSW–SSE at 11–15 kph gusting ~19. Cross to lightly onshore now and staying manageable rather than blown out, but the crisp window has closed. South-facing corners hold the cleanest shape from here.

days.label: Today
days.note: Morning was the session and it has just closed. Solid dead-S groundswell (7.2ft @ 10s, 179°) with clean W offshore at dawn — by 11:40am the wind is SSW–SSE cross and the 9:22am high is draining toward a 2:53pm low. Long Reef is the pick at 6–8ft with real consequence; Curl Curl is the sensible middle at 4–6ft; Dee Why is shadowed at 4–5ft and only the Point bends it; North Steyne is thigh-to-stomach. If you were home, dawn to 10am was it — and you're in Oahu, so this one is for the record.

swells.label: Dead-south mid-period groundswell — the engine today, and the one angle Dee Why is shadowed from
Same source read at the southern end — a second of extra period, heavily shadowed inside Manly

dee-why.window: Dawn to 10am was the window and it has gone. The Point is the only corner that bends a 179° dead-S into a rideable wall — sit wide and let it wrap; the open beachie banks will be closing out. From here the SSE cross takes the shape out of it and the draining tide makes the inside banks shallow.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: Frontside at the Point, which is the only place a 179° swell is worth surfing here. Ten seconds of period carries a lot of push with not much face — take off deeper than feels comfortable and commit to one bottom turn before it fattens on the inside. The wider sets wrapped best around the 9:22am high; on the drain they'll square up on the ledge.

swells.label: Dead-south mid-period groundswell — the engine today, and the one angle Dee Why is shadowed from
Same source read at the southern end — a second of extra period, heavily shadowed inside Manly

long-reef.window: Pick of the coast and by a clear margin — full exposure to the 179° south. Hugh McDowell had it as 'AM for some head to OH clean surf' under W winds, then needing shelter as the wind goes SW then S. Dawn to mid-morning was the go; it is now 8kt SSW and lightly onshore.
alerts: 6–8ft and well overhead on a 10-second dead-S — pick your paddle channel off the headland before you jump in, not after. This is the heaviest water of the four by a long way.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: The Reef corner runs right, so this is your frontside. At 6–8ft on a dead-S the difference between a set wave and a closeout is entirely where you sit — a little further north than the crowd, off the reef edge, so you can use the channel to get back out. Step up on volume, not length.

swells.label: Dead-south mid-period groundswell — the engine today, and the one angle Dee Why is shadowed from
Same source read at the southern end — a second of extra period, heavily shadowed inside Manly

curl-curl.window: The sensible middle — real size and punch without Long Reef's consequence. Was best 7:00–10:00am while the W held straighter offshore here than at Dee Why. North Curl Curl corner holds the cleanest shape now the wind has gone S.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Curl Curl's lefts are your backhand and they need exactly this much swell to bank up — 4–6ft on a dead-S is when they work. Keep your weight forward through the first turn; on a 10-second period the wave outruns you if you stall to set up.

swells.label: Dead-south mid-period groundswell — the engine today, and the one angle Dee Why is shadowed from
Same source read at the southern end — a second of extra period, heavily shadowed inside Manly

manly.window: Shadowed hard — thigh-to-stomach on a swell that is well overhead at Long Reef. Jax Richards notes the mid-period component edging a few degrees toward S-SSE opens a broader range of beaches as the swell settles, but North Steyne is the last to feel it. Only worth the drive if the northern banks look too heavy.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Steyne is the most sheltered of the four and today shows exactly why. If you end up here it is a small-wave backhand session on the lefts — you generate all the speed yourself, the swell won't do it for you. Ride volume, not a step-up.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Today's south swell eases back but Surfline is flagging more south swell inbound for NSW across the weekend, so expect a fresh reinforcement rather than a clean drop-off. Same shape to the day is likely — lightest winds early, onshore building through the afternoon. Long Reef stays the size leader, Dee Why stays shadowed while the swell holds a southerly angle. Tides run low 3:54am, high 9:57am, low 3:35pm, high 9:52pm.

dee-why.window: Morning again. Still a southerly angle, so the Point remains the only corner doing real work — wide sets that wrap, not the open beachie banks. Watch for the swell direction nudging east: every degree off dead-S is worth more here than any amount of extra height.

days.note: Surfline is calling more south swell into the NSW coast across the weekend, so both days should carry rideable size rather than fading out.
